findings.claim: The documented reset does not replace every learner change. setup_lab.py removes only four declared paths, leaves arbitrary learner-created files in the starter repository, and then commits those files through git add --all. cleanup_lab.py also leaves them behind. This makes reset nondeterministic and can silently put a learner note or local data into the rebuilt repository despite the reset promise.

evidence.section: shutil.rmtree: deleting a complete directory tree before deterministic restoration

findings.recommendation: Make reset and cleanup restore the entire starter repository to shipped bytes: containment-check and remove/recreate starter/ship-safe-change (or remove every non-shipped child) before copying fixtures. Add a regression test that creates an arbitrary nested file, reruns setup and cleanup, and proves the file is absent and never enters the initial commit.

findings.claim: The expected initial status is not deterministic under normal learner Git configuration. Git also reads the global core.excludesFile; if it contains the common .env pattern, git status does not list .env as untracked before the learner edits the repository-local .gitignore. The lab currently fixes several local settings but does not override core.excludesFile.

evidence.section: DESCRIPTION: core.excludesFile supplies user-level ignore patterns
core.excludesFile configuration and configuration scope precedence

findings.recommendation: During setup, set repository-local core.excludesFile to a generated empty file inside .git so user-level patterns cannot alter the starting lesson state, while leaving global config unchanged. Add a test that supplies a global excludes file containing .env and still observes .env as initially untracked; alternatively, explicitly teach and accommodate the variation with git check-ignore -v.
